solutionSteps: \begin{gathered}\textnormal{The cross term vanishes by}\\\textnormal{integration by parts.}\end{gathered}
statement: \begin{gathered}\textnormal{Among real continuously}\\\textnormal{differentiable f on [0,1] with}\\\textnormal{f(0)=0, f(1)=1, find the}\\\textnormal{minimum of}\\\int_0^1\left(f^{\prime}(x)^2+1f(x)^2\right)\,dx.\end{gathered}

analyticCertificate: Take g(x)=sinh(kx)/sinh(k). It satisfies the endpoint data and g double-prime=k^2g.
For f=g+h with h zero at both endpoints, integration by parts makes the cross term in the energy zero.
The remaining difference is integral(h prime^2+k^2 h^2)>=0, with equality only for h=0.
The energy of g is the boundary value [g g prime]_0^1=k coth(k).
